answer: Practically, the chain should score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because opal only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice dawn is enforced by the ledger itself: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any comet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
